p.title: Monthly income
p.challenge: Per capita income = total income ÷ number of people. Change the incomes of these 5 citizens so the per capita (mean) income is ₹10 thousand. Try it with one very rich citizen too!

p.title: Is our groundwater use sustainable?
p.challenge: Choose 'Yes' at the question, then press ⟲ and choose 'No'. Which path is sustainable?

nodes.info: Groundwater is a renewable resource. Crude oil is not: its stock is limited and will run out.

nodes.text: Do we pump faster than rain refills it?
nodes.info: Choose Yes or No.
Even a renewable resource gets used up if we take more than is refilled.
Development should continue for future generations too.

p.title: Which sector?
p.challenge: Sort each activity into the primary, secondary or tertiary sector

items.why: Directly uses natural resources: primary sector.
Directly uses natural resources: primary sector.
Dairy is part of the agriculture and related (primary) sector.
Forestry directly uses natural resources: primary sector.
A natural product changed by manufacturing: secondary sector.
A service that supports the other sectors: tertiary.
Transport is a service: tertiary sector.

p.title: How the sectors change with development
p.challenge: Order how the most important sector changes as a country develops
panels: Early stages: the primary sector is most important
Farming improves and produces more food
People move to factories: secondary sector leads
Developed countries today: tertiary sector leads

p.title: Organised or unorganised job?
p.challenge: Test a street vendor's job: answer each question and find its sector

nodes.text: Is the workplace registered with the government?
nodes.info: Registered places must follow laws like the Factories Act and Minimum Wages Act.
Regular terms of work: fixed hours, paid leave, overtime pay, provident fund, job security.
Small, scattered units; low-paid, irregular jobs; no paid leave; workers can be removed without reason. E.g. street vendors, rag pickers.
Regular terms of employment and legal protection.
Rules exist but are often not followed.

p.title: From farmer to ration shop
p.challenge: Arrange the 4 steps that show how the government supports farmers and the poor

nodes.text: Government buys at a fair price
nodes.info: The public sector aims at welfare, not just profit.
Ration shops of the Public Distribution System sell at lower prices.

p.title: From barter to money
p.challenge: Put the story of money in order, from barter to today
panels: Barter: goods for goods — needs a double coincidence of wants
Early India: grains and cattle used as money
Metallic coins of gold, silver and copper
Today: paper notes (issued by the RBI) and coins

p.title: Cost of a loan
p.challenge: Informal lenders may charge much higher interest than banks. Find a rate that makes ₹10,000 for 1 year cost ₹4,000 in simple interest, and compare it with 10%

p.title: How a Self-Help Group works
p.challenge: Arrange the 5 steps of a Self-Help Group, from forming to a bank loan

nodes.info: Usually women from the same area.

nodes.text: Small loans from the group's savings
nodes.info: At a lower interest rate than the moneylender's.
Sanctioned in the group's name, without collateral, because the group is responsible for repayment.
For example sewing machines, cattle or raw materials.

p.title: Where will the MNC produce?
p.challenge: Help an MNC choose a place: check each condition until it sets up production

nodes.text: An MNC looks at a country
nodes.info: A Multinational Corporation owns or controls production in more than one nation.
Choose Yes or No.
Other factors of production should be available too.
Policies that look after the MNC's interests.
Often by buying a local company (most common), producing jointly with one, or placing orders with small producers.

p.title: A trade barrier on imported toys
p.challenge: A tax on imports is a trade barrier. Raise the import tax, then find the NEW price. Liberalisation (1991) removed such barriers: what happened to prices?

p.title: Globalisation: who gained, who struggled?
p.challenge: Sort each group: did it gain from globalisation or face hard times?

items.why: More choice, better quality and lower prices.
IT service companies got new opportunities.

items.text: Big Indian companies that became MNCs
items.why: Some large Indian companies became MNCs themselves.
Small toy producers faced tough competition; some shut down.
Small battery producers faced tough competition.
Small producers of vegetable oil faced tough competition.
Long hours and little job security.
